articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a beautiful 167-vulnerability gift pack including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Because why patch one thing when you can patch ALL THE THINGS?

articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: Linux's 'Dirty Frag' flaw makes CopyFail look quaint—public root exploit, no patches, broken disclosure embargo. Peak infosec comedy right here, folks.

articles.title: The 13 Must-See Broadway Shows to Catch if You’re Visiting NYC This Summer
articles.summary: Ivanti's EPMM gets pwned again with zero-day RCE exploitation in the wild. At this point, 'Ivanti vulnerability' is basically a redundant phrase.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas education platform gets defaced by ransomware crew, disrupting schools nationwide. Nothing says 'back to school' like a good old-fashioned extortion demand on your login page.

articles.title: Free Signal Guide
articles.summary: Russian military intel hackers mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens through compromised routers. Because why break in when you can just steal everyone's keys?

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Meta abandons Instagram DM encryption after years of privacy theater, handing themselves full visibility into user chats. Surveillance capitalism wins again!

articles.title: The SECURE Data Act is Not a Serious Piece of Privacy Legislation
articles.summary: EFF tears apart California's social media age verification scheme as another authoritarian trojan horse. Age gates: the new 'think of the children' excuse for mass surveillance.
